what: Bags, cubic yards or tons of mulch, topsoil, gravel and sand
title: Mulch Calculator: How Much Mulch, Soil or Gravel Do I Need? | Calcupine
description: Calculate cubic yards, bags or tons of mulch, topsoil, gravel or sand for garden beds, paths and patio bases. Works with odd-shaped and round beds.
lede: Pick a material, enter your bed or path size and depth, and see how many bags or cubic yards to get. Round tree rings and curved beds work too.

faq.q: How many bags of mulch are in a cubic yard?
faq.a: A cubic yard is 27 cubic feet. That is 13.5 bags of 2 cu ft mulch, or 9 bags of 3 cu ft.
2 to 3 inches works for most garden beds. Thinner layers let weeds through; much deeper layers can keep roots too wet. Keep mulch pulled back a few inches from tree trunks and stems.

faq.q: How much does a cubic yard of gravel weigh?
faq.a: Roughly 1.3 to 1.5 tons depending on the stone and moisture. The calculator uses 1.4 tons. Suppliers often sell gravel by the ton, so ask them for their own figure.

faq.q: Is bulk mulch cheaper than bags?
faq.a: Usually, once you need more than about 2 cubic yards. Bulk prices are per yard plus a delivery fee, so small jobs can still be cheaper in bags.

faq.q: How much topsoil do I need for a raised bed?
faq.a: Multiply the bed's length by width in feet and by the depth in inches divided by 12. A 4 by 8 foot bed filled 10 inches deep holds about 26.7 cubic feet, close to 1 cubic yard. Many gardeners fill raised beds with a soil and compost blend rather than plain topsoil.
